subject: spanish
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How would you write 'trabajador' to describe a hard-working woman?
questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -dor add -a for the feminine singular, so a hard-working woman is 'trabajadora'.
“Hacer footing” is a borrowed term meaning “to go jogging/running”.
“Equilibrada” = balanced, so “una dieta equilibrada” = “a balanced diet”.
“Soltero” means “single/unmarried”, so “está soltero” = “he is single”.
Temporary states use 'estar': 'Estoy cansado'. 'Casado' means married, a near-miss spelling distractor.
“Embarazada” is a false friend meaning “pregnant”, not “embarrassed” (which is “avergonzado/a”).

questions.q: How do you say “Smoking damages your health”?
questions.explain: “Fumar” = to smoke and “perjudicar la salud” = to damage your health.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'Social media can be dangerous'?
options: Los medios sociales puede ser peligroso
Las redes sociales pueden ser peligrosas
Las redes sociales pueden ser seguras
Las redes sociales son siempre divertidas
questions.explain: 'Las redes sociales' is feminine plural, so 'peligrosas' agrees; 'pueden ser peligrosas' = 'can be dangerous'.
'El correo electrónico' literally 'electronic mail' means 'email'.

questions.q: Which sentence means “The internet keeps me informed”?
questions.explain: “Mantener informado” = “to keep informed”, so “Internet me mantiene informado”.
“Disfrazarse” means “to dress up / wear a costume”, e.g. at carnival.

questions.q: How would you write 'limpio' to describe two beaches ('playas')?
questions.explain: 'Playa' is feminine, so the plural adjective is feminine plural: 'limpias'.

questions.q: Which means “We have been friends since childhood”?
questions.explain: “Desde la niñez” = since childhood and “ser amigos” = to be friends: “Somos amigos desde la niñez”.
'El tabaquismo' is the habit/addiction of smoking, not a shop (that would be 'el estanco').

questions.q: How do you say “I prefer subtitles to dubbing”?
options: Prefiero el doblaje a los subtítulos
Prefiero los subtítulos a la pantalla
questions.explain: “Los subtítulos” = subtitles and “el doblaje” = dubbing: “Prefiero los subtítulos al doblaje”.
“Estar resfriado” means “to have a cold”.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I'm a fan of pop music”?
options: Soy aficionado a la música pop
Estoy aficionado a la música pop
Soy aficionada a la música clásica
questions.explain: “Ser aficionado a” = “to be a fan of”, so “Soy aficionado a la música pop”.
“El tiempo libre” means “free time / leisure time”.

questions.q: Which sentence means “Social media can be addictive”?
options: Las redes sociales puede ser adictivas
Las redes sociales pueden estar adictivas
Las redes sociales pueden ser adictivas
Las redes sociales pueden ser aburridas
questions.explain: “Las redes sociales” = social media and “adictivas” = addictive: “pueden ser adictivas”.
“La muela” means a “molar/back tooth”, so “me duele la muela” = toothache.

questions.q: How do you say “I have blue eyes”?
questions.explain: “Los ojos azules” = blue eyes, so “Tengo los ojos azules”.
“Los sellos” here means “stamps”, so “coleccionar sellos” = “to collect stamps”.
